content.text:
The directory exists locally but there's no `.gitignore` to keep the `.mmd` file out. The fix is two parts:

1. Add a `.gitkeep` so the directory is tracked (CI will have it)
2. Add a `.gitignore` to ignore the generated `.mmd` output

But actually, `docs/plans/` already has committed files in it, so CI already has the directory. The real issue is likely that the test is writing a file that then shows up as an untracked change, or the directory doesn't exist on a fresh clone if those plan files aren't committed on this branch.

content.text:
There it is — `docs/plans/` isn't tracked at all on this branch. It only exists locally. On CI, the directory won't exist and the test will fail with a "no such file or directory" error on `os.WriteFile`.

The cleanest fix: make the test create the directory itself with `os.MkdirAll` before writing. That way it works everywhere without needing to track an empty directory. And we should `.gitignore` the generated output.

content.text:
Only the `.gitignore` itself will be tracked — the `.mmd` output is ignored. Here's what changed:

1. **`phase_test.go`** — Changed output path from `docs/plans/` to `docs/generated/`, and added `os.MkdirAll` so the directory is created at test time (no dependency on it pre-existing).

2. **`docs/generated/.gitignore`** — Ignores everything in the directory except itself. The `.gitignore` gets committed (so the directory exists on CI), but generated `.mmd` files won't.
